item.title: Re: A theory
item.content:encoded:
So, when I write an article like this, I often have a working theory about what's going on. However, I want to emphasize: My working theory isn't something you're supposed to 'get' out of the article. My goal was to establish atmosphere and mood; the theory I worked with was just to maintain consistency.

In other words: don't take the following break-down too seriously. It's not something I'd expect any reader to 'get' from the article I wrote; it's just the head-canon I was using that informed a lot of my decisions.

Spoilers.
– hide block

Let's look at each movie: Nichts (Nothing), a movie about exploring a massive munitions factory (wherein, among other things, a dreidel is found). Doppelgänger (Doppelganger), a movie about being pursued by one's own dark reflection. Schuld (Guilt), a movie that shows people being burned on a pyre and somehow inspires feelings of physical illness and anxiety in anyone who watches it. And finally, the titular Abwesenheit (Absence), a movie we know little about, but was Hellmuth's last work (and, prior to Ottinger, presumed lost).

Now, let's look at Hellmuth's letter. In it, he states:

The author must be obliterated down to their elemental structure, down to their essence, their very core. No trace of their presence can remain on this earth. The author must cease to be.

A central motif of his work, then, is this hostile view of the author: The author is an enemy that must either be destroyed, or presumed to have never existed in the first place. Secondary themes involve guilt, despair, isolation, and self-loathing. So… what's this all about? What's going on?

Well, when and where were these movies produced? Hellmuth is clearly German. All his movies are dated in the 1950s and 60s, in post-War Germany — during a period when Germans were experiencing a sort of collective guilt (or Kollektivschuld) over the Holocaust and surrounding atrocities perpetuated by the Nazi party.

Remember the dreidel in Nichts?

In Nichts, Hellmuth films a German munitions factory abandoned after WW2. In Doppelgänger, Hellmuth is pursued by a dark reflection of himself — the reflection of a self that would permit something like the Holocaust to happen. In Schuld, Hellmuth expresses the guilt and revulsion that consumes him (prior to its modern meaning, 'holocaust' was a Jewish sacrificial rite involving a burnt offering). And finally, in Abwesenheit, Hellmuth made real his final desire to vanish into the horror (doesn't that last frame look like it's taking place in a facility, somewhere? A facility with barbed wire? With a single figure standing at the door?).

There's an entire branch of Jewish theology dedicated to whether or not God died in the Holocaust. This is Hellmuth's central thesis: In the wake of the Holocaust, God must either not exist… or be destroyed. God is either dead, or a monster. And what is a film-maker but the God of their own little world? Hellmuth chose non-existence. He chose Abwesenheit.

Enter Basil Ottinger: A slimy little art collector who just wouldn't let Hellmuth go. He kept digging, learning everything he could about this guy. He even went as far as acquiring a copy of the very movie Hellmuth never wanted the world to see (the fire that claimed Abwesenheit was no accident).

For Hellmuth, being an artist in the wake of something as terrible as the Holocaust was impossible… so, he chose to vanish into his little world. But Basil wouldn't let him vanish. Basil wanted to meet him. Basil wanted to know the God of this little world — the dark reflection that would permit something like the Holocaust to exist.

And, in the end…?

He got his wish.

item.title: A theory
item.content:encoded:
Spoilers(?) ahead, be warned

+ show block
– hide block

Doppelgänger was Hellmuth’s fifth film. Assuming no films between Doppelgänger and Schuld were made, and none between Schuld and Abwesenheit, then Abwesenheit was Hellmuth’s seventh film. Hellmuth’s films frequently feature themes of darkness and oblivion (according to Google Translate, nichts=nothing, abwesenheit=absence), and perhaps the number seven may have triggered something strange...

Alternatively...
Collapse collapsible

Abwesenheit is German for absence. Maybe the idea is that that’s the point. Hellmuth believed that the author must not exist. Abwesenheit is the absence of a film, and possibly its director.

item.title: Re: *spooky ghost noises*
item.content:encoded:
If anyone wants to write for this, here's some basic things you might want to consider.

Keep in mind, this is entirely my own interpretation (and represents only what I and I alone am trying to do with this). There is no canon, etc etc:

  • Think of Parawatch as the Velma Dinkleys of the SCP-verse. They are spooky ghost-nerds who swap creepy camp-fire stories on the internet while remaining utterly oblivious to the Foundation's existence. In short, they are us.
  • Seriously, imagine Ghost Hunters. These are the people who clock a hundred hours into studying a "haunted house" on account of once seeing a "spooky face" in a window. If they were ever to meet a Foundation agent, this is how it would go down.
  • Think of it as a chance to write classic creepypasta from a POV that doesn't know about the Foundation. My aim here is to reproduce that pre-2000 "I run this website out of my cousin's garage" energy that creepypasta used to have. Think Killswitch. Think Lenentine Cards. Think Dionaea House. Heck, think the wiki's own Manistique Broadcast. In short: Think small. Think low-key. Think subtle. For just one moment, get the reader to wonder: "wait — is this for real?"
  • Lore is the enemy. I do not know who these people are — and I do not care to find out. They are a thinly disguised delivery mechanism for creepypastas in the SCP-verse. The less we know about them, the better this works.
  • Most importantly: I shouldn't have to know anything about the SCP-verse to enjoy it. That's my primary aim here — to write something in the SCP-verse that is fun and spooky, but doesn't require even a baseline understanding of the SCP-verse to enjoy.

Life itself is only a vision. A dream.
Nothing exists, save empty space and you.
And you...

...are but a thought.

My attempt at a pure, classical styled creepy-pasta.
